item.title: Refreshed Maro Itoje leads from the front as England deliver performance they needed
item.description: Moses Itoje must wonder what all the fuss was about. The newborn son of Maro and his wife had his first taste of Twickenham on Sunday afternoon, perhaps the youngest of the nearly 82,000-strong crowd at the Allianz Stadium that watched England rack up a record score against Australiia. For a player who was supposed to be resting and recharging after a gruelling physical and emotional year, one might question the wisdom of welcoming a child so close to the autumn opener. “My sleep is okay actually,” Itoje chuckled this week from the safety of England’s training base. “My wife's sleep is a bit more challenging, but she's doing a good job.” Maro Itoje (right) with his wife Mimi (left) and newborn son (Reuters) No doubt the England captain played like a man enjoying the restorative benefits of a break. It had been a bold call to allow Itoje the summer off given the juncture at which he exited, having presided over a worst-ever Six Nations. But here was a call made with long-term goals in mind . As captain of Saracens, England and the British and Irish Lions, the 32-year-old lock has been afforded precious little time off across more than a decade at Test level – indeed, his durability has counted against him, with no major injuries of which to speak. How, then, did it feel to be back pulling on an England shirt for the first time in months? “I’ve absolutely loved it. Sometimes when you have time away – and I do think it was a good thing for me personally – it just lights the fire in you a little bit. It just makes you more appreciative of the opportunity and the platform that you have when you play for England. It is something that I don’t take for granted. As many games as I have left, I want to make the absolute most of it.” Itoje was a menace throughout the game against Australia (Getty) Itoje played with that intent. Like a nosy (and noisy) neighbour peering over the fence, he timed his hassling and harrying of Ryan Lonergan superbly – getting his hands to an early box kick and up in the face of the Wallabies scrum half repeatedly. England’s captain topped the tackle charts with 16, plenty of them made before the interval in an outstanding defensive effort; at half-time, the hosts had made 75 tackles and missed just two. With plenty of focus on the battle at the breakdown, Australia were simply beaten up. Itoje and Ben Curry – influential on his return to Test duty – led the way, largely keeping their discipline as they pilfered and pawed, bar one over-balance from the England skipper. Poor Declan Meredith, the inexperienced Australia fly half, had little ball passed his way; when it did arrive, it was wobbly, and Meredith rather had the look of a seasick sailor treading an unsteady deck. “I guess they made every ruck a mess,” the captain Harry Wilson admitted. item.title: Winchester City Flyers 3-3 Reading Women: Match Report
item.description: Lara Moore on the ball with Keziah Banduka (left), Ellie Szekeres (centre) and Poppy Whitburn (right) watching on / | Alison Matthews Reading Women and Winchester City Flyers played out a thrilling six-goal encounter at the Charters Community Stadium on Sunday, with the Royals having to settle for a frustrating 3-3 draw despite producing a remarkable comeback. Similar to other recent matches, the Royals found themselves on the back foot after just 10 minutes. The hosts raced into an early 2-0 lead through a headed finish from Charlie Snelling and a close-range effort from Vinnie Nkomo. However, Reading once again showed incredible resilience and character to fight their way back into the contest. Alice Curr’s eighth goal of the season began the revival before Bogi Tramontini struck to bring the Royals level – in a deserved comeback – with Reading wondering how they weren’t ahead at the break with the scores locked at 2-2. Reading continued to push after the break and were rewarded just after the hour mark when Tramontini broke through to grab her second goal of the afternoon, completing a remarkable turnaround to put the Royals 3-2 ahead. With the clock running down, Reading looked to have done enough to secure all three points, only for Flyers’ Snelling to score her second headed goal from a corner, leaving the Royals team to reflect on a hard-fought comeback, but also an ultimately frustrating and arguably disappointing 3-3 draw. I am sure that, come Tuesday morning (allowing for Ed Jackson-Norris’ 24 hours of ‘wallow time’), the focus will turn towards the positives to take from the performance, alongside addressing the areas of weakness exposed during the match. Emma Pearmine has once again assembled a competitive Winchester City Flyers side, and one that looks more than capable of challenging for the league title after finishing second in the 2025/26 campaign, just a single point behind Wycombe Wanderers. The Flyers have certainly proved to be something of a nemesis for Reading over the Royals’ last two seasons in tier five, having won all four of their previous meetings. Sunday’s draw, and disappointment at the end of the match, highlights the continued improvements and expectations of the team, with Reading finally taking points off their ‘thorn in the side’ rivals. With just four points separating the top six, the league table is already shaping up to be as competitive and closely contested as anticipated. All of the six teams will have their sights firmly set on challenging for top spot, meaning every point could prove crucial. While Sunday’s result will undoubtedly feel like two points dropped after such a determined comeback, at the end of the season, this hard-earned point against one of the league’s strongest teams may prove to be a valuable one in Reading’s promotion challenge. item.title: Journalist explains how Bernardo Silva is becoming Real Madrid’s new midfield conductor: ‘He isn’t Modric, but…’
item.description: Journalist explains how Bernardo Silva is becoming Real Madrid’s new midfield conductor: ‘He isn’t Modric, but…’ Bernardo Silva is gradually establishing himself as an important figure in Real Madrid’s midfield, with his performances attracting praise from journalist Mario Cortegana. The Portuguese midfielder arrived with considerable expectations, particularly because of the experience and technical quality he could bring to a team searching for greater creativity and control in possession. Although comparisons with Luka Modric were inevitable, Cortegana says the Portuguese is developing a different role under Jose Mourinho. Speaking on his YouTube channel , Cortegana highlighted the midfielder’s ability to connect Real Madrid’s different departments and give direction to their attacking play. Why Bernardo Silva is important to Real Madrid Bernardo was initially viewed as an experienced addition capable of addressing Real Madrid’s midfield shortcomings. Bernardo Silva is slowly finding his rhythm at Real Madrid. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) However, his arrival was not universally convincing, particularly with fans expecting the club to pursue a more traditional creative midfielder such as Rodri or Martin Zubimendi. Nevertheless, Cortegana believes the Portuguese international is gradually demonstrating why his signing makes sense. “Bernardo Silva isn’t Modric, but without being brilliant, he’s weaving Real Madrid’s football together to give it meaning; his partnership with Tchouaméni is really taking hold.” Bernardo’s partnership with Tchouameni improves Madrid’s midfield One of Bernardo’s most important contributions has been his developing relationship with Aurelien Tchouameni , which comes after Mourinho has decided to use Federico Valverde in defence. The Frenchman provides defensive protection and physical presence, while Bernardo offers the technical qualities needed to progress possession and connect attacks. Bernardo has benefited from Valverde’s move to the right-back spot. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Cortegana specifically highlighted the Portuguese midfielder’s influence on Madrid’s build-up, explaining that “Bernardo makes passes, makes runs off the ball, and gives meaning to the game with those small details. “Neither Tchouameni, nor Fede Valverde, nor Camavinga have that ability to build play.” Modric comparisons explain Bernardo’s growing influence Replacing Luka Modric was never going to be straightforward for the player nor for Real Madrid. The Croatian’s technical quality, vision and influence over several successful Real Madrid teams established an exceptionally high standard. Hence, Bernardo should not be judged against Modric’s entire career, although there are similarities in the way both players help organise possession and provide direction when their teams need greater control.

item.title: Gary Neville singles out FOUR players who will get Manchester United relegated after defensive disaster against Aston Villa
item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United legend Gary and Phil Neville have delivered a scathing assessment of the club’s current defensive options following a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. The former stars believe the lack of recruitment in the backline has left the Red Devils in a perilous position that could threaten their top-flight status. Chaotic eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford United went into the November international break sitting 18th in the Premier League after a disastrous defensive display. The hosts found themselves two goals down within five minutes courtesy of rapid strikes from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson. Michael Carrick's men rallied before the break, drawing level through a Bruno Fernandes penalty and a goal from former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans. However, the visitors regained control after the restart with a Josh McGinn penalty and a fourth from Leon Goretzka. Staring at a damaging defeat, United salvaged a point in injury time. Substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu struck late on to secure a 4-4 draw , sparing the club from dropping to the bottom of the table. Neville brothers blast defensive options The match ended with a makeshift backline consisting of Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven, and Dorgu. Speaking on NBC Sports , Gary Neville pointed to the club's summer transfer activity as the root cause of the chaos. "The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window," he said. "Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake. The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors… we all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in. They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in." His brother Phil shared the same sentiment, singling out the closing defensive quartet. "The back-four that finished the game - Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven and Dorgu - that gets you relegated," he added. "That back-four gets you the sack as a manager and that back-four cannot keep United, I don’t think, in the Premier League. That back-four gets you relegated, it’s poor. It’s not good enough to play in the Premier League." Deep-rooted institutional problems The draw leaves United suffering an eight-game winless league run, plunging them to their lowest position at this stage of a campaign since 1986. Despite this grim reality, Neville insists that sacking Carrick would not solve the wider systemic issues at Old Trafford. "You can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce," the former captain added. item.title: ‘Held My Breath For a Second,’ ‘We Can’t Have Anything Good’ — NFL World Taken Aback By Footage of Eagles LB’s Nasty Hit on J.J. McCarthy
item.description: ‘Held My Breath For a Second,’ ‘We Can’t Have Anything Good’ — NFL World Taken Aback By Footage of Eagles LB’s Nasty Hit on J.J. McCarthy The New York Giants picked up a 19-11 win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, with J.J. McCarthy leading the team at quarterback. McCarthy faced constant pressure from the Eagles’ defense, which brought him down for five sacks. Notably, McCarthy’s performance was also interrupted by a frightening moment in the third quarter. He took a brutal hit to his lower abdomen in the third quarter when Eagles linebacker Zack Baun led with his helmet while attempting to stop the QB’s run. It ultimately made direct contact with McCarthy’s side as Baun brought him down, triggering reactions from the NFL community. J.J. McCarthy’s Painful Collision With Zack Baun Leaves the NFL World Worried After the brutal play, McCarthy attempted a few warm-up throws to determine whether he could continue. He winced in pain after his first attempt and collapsed to the ground in considerable discomfort following the second. The medical staff later escorted McCarthy to the locker room for further evaluation. Reacting to the footage, KDKA-TV sports director Bob Pompeani compared the collision to a similar incident involving Mike Tomczak and Tracy Scroggins. “J. J. McCarthy turned into a massive hit. It reminded me of Mike Tomczak turning into Tracy Scroggins and getting blindsided in a 1995 game. Tomczak suffered a bruised sternum,” Pompeani wrote . “Dang,” popular analyst/ host Trey Wingo wrote . McCarthy later explained that the play was designed as a quarterback run, but his decision to pull the ball back inside after reading the defense left him exposed to Baun. He acknowledged that he spotted the linebacker late and attempted to lower his shoulder to absorb the contact, but failed to get low enough. McCarthy also credited Baun for delivering an excellent hit and accepted responsibility, saying that he needed to do a better job of protecting himself in such situations. Meanwhile, reactions to the hit continued. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “JJ McCarthy ran into a WALL on this one. Held my breath for a second,” Anthony Rivardo, host of the Fireside Giants, wrote . “The guy is just so small, man… naturally, the first non-scramble rushing attempt he has as a starter ends in him leaving the game. We can’t have anything good. Not one thing,” Justin Penik, host of the “Talkin’ Giants” podcast, wrote . McCarthy managed to return to the game just before the end of the third quarter and remained optimistic about his condition, insisting he would be fine. But his recovery could become a concern for the Giants, who are scheduled to face the Washington Commanders on Thursday. With McCarthy initially listed as questionable to return, the Giants turned to Jameis Winston under center. Winston, who ranks No. 23 in the PFN QB Impact with a 70.5 grade, led the offense on a touchdown drive before returning to the sideline.

Harrison Butker missed two field goals in the first half against the New York Jets, drawing loud boos from the home crowd at Arrowhead Stadium. The veteran kicker acknowledged the fans’ frustration after Kansas City’s 35-12 victory and admitted he has been just as critical of himself. “I’m booing myself sometimes. People are passionate. item.description: STORRS — As highlights flickered across the video board and the crowd at Gampel Pavilion rose to its feet, Azzi Fudd paused beneath the championship banners she helped add to the rafters, soaking in the cheers one more time. The former UConn star smiled, waved and embraced those closest to her on Sunday afternoon. Fudd was back at center stage in Storrs , only this time not as a player chasing history, but as the newest member of the Huskies of Honor. Just two seasons removed from helping UConn capture a national championship, Fudd was honored just before the Huskies’ game against Iowa. Former Huskies Alisha Clark, Gabby Williams, Tina Charles and Tiffany Hayes were all in attendance. Despite battling injuries throughout her college career, Fudd completed her time at Storrs as one of the program’s defining players. Her induction into the Huskies of Honor solidifies her legacy as one of UConn’s most storied players. item.title: Halling, 200 freestyle relay team qualifies for state finals
item.description: OTSEGO — The Sturgis swim and dive team had a strong showing at the conference finals this past weekend. Sturgis finished third overall as a team at the SCC Conference Meet hosted by the Otsego Aquatic Center. The Trojans finished with 296 points. Harper Creek won the conference finals while piling up 555 points at the event. South Haven finished just ahead of Sturgis in third with 324. The good news for Sturgis was a pair of state-qualifying swims. MUSICAL TIME: 'Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat' coming to Sturgis VOLLEYBALL ENDS: Volleyball seasons end for Sturgis, Three Rivers in district play Katelyn Halling registered an individual state cut in the 50 freestyle on Friday. She posted 25.83 seconds in that race. On Saturday, she finished third in the 50 free final at 26.08 seconds, that also would have been a state time. Halling also helped Sturgis qualify for the state finals in the 200 freestyle relay. The team had been attempting go log a state cut in that race all season. It finally came on their last attempt as they posted a time of 1:46.60 to finish second overall at the conference finals. Halling teamed up with Sydney Herblet, Lilly Whitehead and Ainsley Gump in that race. Sturgis finished with several all-conference swims on the weekend. Gump won the 200 individual medley race at 2:13.69. The 200 medley relay team of Brooklyn Draper, Whitehead, Gump and Halling swam to second place overall at 1:58.19. Sturgis also had a consolation finalist time of 2:45.31 with the team of Chiara Guiduzzi, Makenna Holden, Haylee Trine and Nele Strasen swimming to 16th. Herblet finished fourth overall in the 200 freestyle race at 2:12.76. Mia Feyes took home ninth at 2:20.78. In the 200 IM, Draper swam to ninth at 2:33.77. For the 50 freestyle, Whitehead was 10th at 27.81 seconds, Ella Whitehead finished 13th at 28.80. Ava Albarran posted 1:27.22 for 15th in the 100 butterfly. The 100 freestyle saw Halling finish fifth at 59.22 seconds. In the lengthy 500 freestyle, Herblet came in fifth place overall at 5:56.04. The Sturgis team of Draper, Albarran, Feyes and Ella Whitehead swam to seventh in the 200 freestyle relay. That group posted a time of 1:56.31. In 100 backstroke racing, Feyes earned an all-conference time of 1:15.75 for eighth place. The 100 breaststroke race saw Gump finish second at 1:09.11, Lilly Whitehead was third overall with a time of 1:14.51 and Ella Whitehead was sixth overall at 1:16.47. Sturgis earned an all-conference swim in the 400 freestyle relay. The team of Ella Whitehead, Albarran, Feyes and Herblet clocked a time of 4:26.23 to finish eighth. item.title: Oviedo sack Calero: Raúl González will be the new manager
item.description: Oviedo sack Calero: Raúl González will be the new manager Not even Real Oviedo’s victory at the Nuevo Mirandilla was enough to save Julián Calero. Despite taking three points against Cádiz and putting Oviedo firmly in the hunt for the promotion play-off places, Grupo Pachuca has decided to part ways with him. In his place, the Asturian club’s majority shareholder has turned to Raúl González Blanco to take charge and lead the push for promotion to the top flight, following the end of his spell with Real Madrid’s academy and reserve team. Calero’s future was already hanging by a thread before the trip to Cádiz following two particularly painful setbacks. The first came in the Copa del Rey, where Numancia (from the Segunda Federación) knocked the Blues out on penalties after a 3-3 draw that exposed serious defensive weaknesses. Days later, defeat to UD Las Palmas at the Carlos Tartiere shattered what confidence remained. The victory over Cádiz was not enough to restore the board’s faith. Jesús Martínez made the coach’s dismissal official on Monday, paving the way for Raúl’s new project. For the Real Madrid legend, this opportunity marks his first managerial role in professional football after his lengthy development spell at La Fábrica and in charge of Real Madrid Castilla. item.title: Auto racing - Lime Rock Park announces 2027 major events schedule
item.description: The schedule for eight major racing and car events in 2027 has been released by Lime Rock Park in Lakeville, Connecticut, set to celebrate its 70th anniversary. Lime Rock has been a prime 1.5-mile road racing course since 1957 and regularly hosts professional and amateur racing events and shows. The United States Auto Club Mustang Cup will lead off on May 14-15 (with free admission) followed by the Trans Am Memorial Day Classic from May 27-30 — also taking place are the American V8s, SVRA Invitational, International GT and Prototype America, plus Royals Garage Car Show. The Sports Car Club of America New England Regionals will be hosted June 11-12 (the first day is free). The summer schedule begins with the LIUNA 150 NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series and ARCA Menards Series weekend on July 9-10. The Gridlife Circuit Legends will appear Aug. 20-21. The Labor Day weekend will have the Historic Festival 45 from Sept. 2-6 - in 2026, 287 competition entries and 1,200 vehicles took part. The Friday, Saturday and Monday cards feature vintage racing, and Sunday in the Park features the Lime Rock Concourse and Gathering of the Marques showcase. The fall schedule will have the FCP Euro Northeast Grand Prix event for IMSA on Sept. 23-25. The MiataCon will take place Oct. 29-30, celebrating Mazda's MX-5 roadster — more than 1,100 Miatas took part in the 2026 event. Tickets go on sale on Monday, Nov. 9, with season passes and Insiders Club passes available for purchase. The track announces general admission ticket prices for the major events remain unchanged from 2026 and reduced gate admission for the Trans Am Memorial Day Classic. "Celebrating 70 years of Lime Rock Park is an incredible milestone, and we're entering this anniversary season with tremendous momentum,'' said Dicky Riegel, the Park President and CEO. "The growth we've experienced across our major events, particularly with grassroots motorsports and enthusiast driven weekends, speaks to the passion of our fans and the strength of the motorsports community. With an expanded schedule, the return of IMSA and our commitment to keeping events accessible and affordable, we're looking forward to making our 70th season one to remember.'' Additional events will be released at a later date. Middletown, in the heart of Orange County, is 50 miles from Lime Rock, and Poughkeepsie is 38 miles away. item.title: The Scott Stecher standard is brave new world for Woodmore football
item.description: You don't want to be the group that doesn't go 10-0. That's what assistant coach Seth Dufendock meant when he reminded Woodmore players that was now the standard. The departing seniors helped make sure of it, before a 28-0 setback to visiting Delta in the second round of the postseason in Division VI. Woodmore, which had never hosted a game in the playoffs, was unbeaten in the regular season for the first time since 1995 and second time in program history. It had a first-round bye after winning the Sandusky Bay Conference championship for the first league crown since 1997. High school football Woodmore football eliminated in second round of OHSAA postseason The Wildcats were 2-8 three years ago, before coach Scott Stecher's arrival. They were 5-5 and 7-4, including a postseason setback his first two seasons. The response from the community warms Stecher's heart. "It brought football back to a place where Friday nights here are a happening," he said. "This hasn't been done in 30 years — all this stuff. We want to keep it rolling." Stecher felt embraced from the start. He wasn't sure he'd get another chance at a program's helm, after his final year at Monroeville in 2020. He was then an assistant at a few stops before Woodmore. "It means the world to me," he said. "It makes me more a believer that God puts you where he wants you. Being part of a football family again has been an awesome blessing. Seeing the kids grow and the community pride." This iteration was the most selfless team Stecher has ever coached. "These kids are high character, good kids," he said. "We had to get them a little meaner, tougher. They're loving, caring. The servant leadership was outstanding teaching young kids. That brought them this far. This group cares about each other." Sophomore running back/linebacker Lucas Caldwell isn't the only one who is already anxious to try to uphold the standard next season. The returners will be a little more battle tested and got a taste of what it takes in Week 12. "He's a one of a kind football player, and his character," Stecher said. "He's fun to be around. I look forward to it." Maybe they'll establish another standard by winning a home playoff game. "We'll work so much harder to do everything we can to be better than this year," Caldwell said. "Knowing the guys that are leaving, they did so much for us.
